messages:
incident-bot: Paging @eng-oncall -> oncall: high error rate on /v1/generate, 2m sustained. Incident severity: P1.
ops-bot: Alert: 5xx spike from gw-cluster (1047 errors/min). Link: https://monitor/redwood/alerts/1845678901
marie: I'm on it — digging into queues & autoscale. First call: <5m. Anyone already saw a customer report?
alex_g: Got a DM from account team — 2 enterprise customers reported timeouts around 16:12 UTC. They saw ~10% failure for long-context requests.
sre_miguel: Looking at GPU pool metrics. pool=rt-gpu-prod shows 97% active, queue depth up to 420 in the last 3m. HPA not scaling fast enough.
marie: Can you paste HPA and scaler events? suspect warmup delay on new nodes + pod init time.
sre_miguel: Here are HPA events:
```
kubectl get hpa rt-inference -o yaml
metrics:
  currentCPUUtilizationPercentage: 82
  desiredReplicas: 18
  currentReplicas: 12
events:
  - reason: ScaleUp
    message: New nodes requested at 2026-04-21T16:09:30Z
```
marie: So desired jumped to 18 but we only had 12 live replicas for ~180s. Warmup / prepull maybe blocked.
eng_lead_jess: We recently changed the node-pool autoscaler cooldown from 60s to 300s for cost reasons — could be related.
alex_g: Customers on dedicated workloads had fallback to smaller model which succeeded, hosted customers hit timeouts.
sre_miguel: Logs from router show backlog growth and OOM retries:
```
[16:10:12] router: enqueue request id=abc123, model=redwood-llama-70b, tokens=4096, queue_len=350
[16:11:05] router: backlog 410, dropped=0, routing_delay_ms=1200
[16:11:30] worker-5: pod crashLoopBackOff on init, reason=nvml timeout
```
marie: Hypothesis 1: HPA desired replicas increased but node provisioning + GPU warmup (driver + model cache) caused effective capacity lag => queue depth spike and client timeouts.
marie: Hypothesis 2: Recent kernel upgrade on node pool increased driver init time; need to check last infra deploy.
eng_lead_jess: Also check our KVS cache hit rate — if warmed KV cache isn't available, cold-hosts served larger compute per request worsening saturation.
sre_miguel: KV cache hit rate dropped from 86% to 12% starting 16:07 (coincident with first HPA event).
marie: Immediate mitigations: 1) scale up a warm node group manually with prewarmed pods, 2) reduce batch size/config for queued requests to lower per-token latency, 3) enable fallback to quantized model for >2k tokens.
alex_g: I'm already patching a routing rule to divert long-context requests to the smaller quantized variant as a temporary safety. Pushed at 16:15.
ops-bot: Deploybot: Route patch applied: route=/v1/generate param.max_context>2048 -> model=redwood-llama-70b-quant-fallback.
marie: After routing change, tail latency improved for long tails, error rate dropped from 11% to 3% in 10m window. Queue depth down to ~120.
sre_miguel: Manual warm node group creation started at 16:20; 6 prewarmed pods came up by 16:26. Effective capacity back to desired.
eng_lead_jess: Good. For postmortem we need timeline, root cause options, and follow-ups: reduce node autoscaler cooldown? prewarm policy? better HPA signal (queue depth vs CPU)?
marie: Assigning action owners:
- miguel: collect node init/warmup logs, NVML driver timings, and kernel upgrade history (owner: @sre_miguel).
- alex_g: route rollback plan + measure customer impact per org (owner: @alex_g).
- jess: evaluate autoscaler cooldown and cost tradeoffs (owner: @eng_lead_jess).
- marie: assemble timeline + KV cache regression analysis (owner: @marie).
marie: Miguel — paste the relevant node events and driver logs here when you have them. Also include `kubectl describe nodes` output for affected nodes.
sre_miguel: Pasting condensed node events:
```
Node i-0a1b2c3: boot 16:07:12, kubelet started 16:07:15, nvidia-driver init start 16:07:33, driver ready 16:08:45
Node i-0d4e5f6: boot 16:09:40, driver init failed 16:09:55 -> retry -> ready 16:11:20
```
sre_miguel: Driver init variance ~70-90s on newly provisioned nodes; model cache pull another ~30-60s depending on layer cache.
marie: That aligns with ~180s effective lag between desired and available replicas. Root cause looks like combined: autoscaler cooldown + slow GPU driver/model warmup + KV cache cold misses.
eng_lead_jess: Agreed. For the RCA include: timeline, contributing factors, mitigation chronology, and recommendations: prewarm pool, HPA signal tuning to include queue depth, revert cooldown change or add burst policy, improve driver init robustness, KV cache persistent snapshot.
alex_g: For customers: drafting an incident summary and outreach plan. I'll attach affected org ids.
marie: On-call handoff: I'm staying until 17:00 to verify stability. If I'm offline, @sre_miguel take over. Leaving notes in ops runbook.
ops-bot: Oncall handoff recorded: marie -> sre_miguel at 16:50 UTC.
sre_miguel: Will collate logs and start RCA doc. Posting initial artifact link: https://docs.redwood/rca/1845678901 (will update).
marie: Thanks all — keep this thread for timeline/hypotheses only. We'll open a postmortem thread later. :thumbsup:
